doc.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021

title: A multiracial band and dancers
summary: Allen says all races passed through the band, and there were many dancers from across the States.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: If a Caucasian musician was attracted to Sun Ra’s music and showed up like you did at a rehearsal, would he have been invited, or she, to, like into the band?
Yeah. I had the United Nations band in the band. People from — Arabs and Englishmen and Africans, everybody on the planet has been through this band. I mean all the races in the planet.
I’m pleased to hear that. Was there a reason that — was there more women in the band over the years?
They were dancers. And we had quite a few dancers. We’d use a certain amount each time. We had dancers from all over the States.
